mbm-2751.clue: I run with one purple lace.
mbm-2751.quote: My little sister gave me three different laces and dared me to choose two. I picked purple and yellow. Every time I look down on a hard hill it feels like somebody in my corner is throwing confetti.

mbm-2752.clue: My old belt is tied round a book now.
mbm-2752.quote: When I outgrew my old belt I wrapped it round the sketchbook where I drew my first forms. The knot still fits my hands. Untie it and you can see all the poses where I forgot which leg was mine.

mbm-2753.clue: The record sleeve has a ring of water on it.
mbm-2753.quote: I put my glass down on the DJ's spare sleeve and left a mark. She drew a little dancer inside the ring, with one toe balanced on the stain. It hangs over the mixer whenever our song comes on.

mbm-2754.clue: Rain is the cheapest filter I've used.
mbm-2754.quote: I took a portrait of my best friend through the wet window of a bus shelter. One drop made her blue earring look like a bright round planet. She calls the photo her official astronaut portrait.

mbm-2755.quote: I read in the courtyard till the shadows reach the blue corner of my towel. I made a bookmark from a few strands of its woven fringe. When I unroll the towel the next sunny afternoon, I know right where to start.

mbm-2756.clue: My volunteer gets to keep the knot.
mbm-2756.quote: I twist two silk ribbons together behind my back and pull out one tidy bow. At my first show a kid asked for the bow to tie his mum's hair. I packed extra ribbons after that.

mbm-2757.clue: I visit the first page on birthdays.
mbm-2757.quote: I read one favorite book every birthday and write the year's date lightly beside the first line. The margins are getting full. The boy in that first penciled date still knows how the adventure ends.

mbm-2758.clue: I shop with a little packet of pepper.
mbm-2758.quote: I collect old salt shakers. A pinch of pepper shows me if the holes still work. At the flea market I once sneezed so loud the vendor threw in a handkerchief.

mbm-2759.clue: My grandpa taught me to putt through lunch.
mbm-2759.quote: Grandpa stood two crusts of bread up as a tiny gate and rolled an olive between them. I practiced on the table until the olive ended up in my soup. The next day I sank the short putt.

mbm-2760.clue: I mind the rope with the yellow ribbon.
mbm-2760.quote: In our bell tower I learned the changes by following one yellow ribbon tied near the rope tail. When I had the pattern right the tower captain let me untie it. I keep it tucked in my score.

mbm-2761.clue: My darkroom has a guest star.
mbm-2761.quote: I hung a little paper star on a thread above the wash tray. It trembles when anyone opens the door. My niece thinks it comes out at night to check the stars in all my prints.

mbm-2762.clue: I keep my ears ahead of my pencil.
mbm-2762.quote: I heard a reed warbler long before I could see it. I filled half a page with the tune in squiggles. When the bird finally appeared I had to squeeze its tiny portrait into the margin.

mbm-2763.clue: The guidebook says to look up, but I looked through.
mbm-2763.quote: A stone bridge had a hole worn smooth in the parapet. Through it I could see one yellow laundry line across the river. I made my own postcard of that private little view.

mbm-2764.clue: I take two clocks to the park.
mbm-2764.quote: One chess clock keeps the game; the kitchen timer in my basket keeps us from burning the cornbread at home. When the little red tomato rings the board goes into the box, even in check.

mbm-2765.clue: I have a rangefinder made of string.
mbm-2765.quote: I use a length of blue string on the practice green to see how far my putts drift. My son winds it round a spool like he's bringing a kite home. He is always rooting for a longer walk.

mbm-2766.clue: My first solo started in the broom cupboard.
mbm-2766.quote: I was too nervous to show our marimba group the tune I'd made. The caretaker heard me play it alone and began whistling it while he swept. When he came past the next rehearsal everyone picked up their mallets and played along.

mbm-2767.clue: The lighthouse keeps one window dark.
mbm-2767.quote: I pieced a lighthouse into a quilt for my cousin. The panes are yellow except the smallest, where I used his navy work shirt. He says that's the room where the keeper finally gets some sleep.

mbm-2768.clue: The corners of our table have names.
mbm-2768.quote: We play porch dominoes so often the varnish is worn away in four places. My dad knows who sits at each corner from the shape of the elbow mark. Mine has a little coffee ring for a halo.

mbm-2769.clue: Our first paying customer wanted the receipt.
mbm-2769.quote: At an outdoor juggling show a little kid dropped a drawing of a coin into my hat. I folded a receipt out of a second drawing and tossed it through my pattern to him. He went home with the striped ball drawn on one side of the paper.

mbm-2770.clue: My skydiving map has a thumb-sized orchard.
mbm-2770.quote: I drew the square orchard I saw under my canopy on the back of a receipt. My friend grows apples there. I gave him the little map and he paid for it with one that filled my whole palm.

mbm-2771.clue: I put the shadow down before the flower.
mbm-2771.quote: My neighbour set her last tulip on my table. While I mixed red, the sun moved and its shadow slid across my sketch. I painted the shadow first so the flower would have somewhere soft to stand.

mbm-2772.clue: The holes in my belt make a song.
mbm-2772.quote: I punch leather belts in pairs and tap a tune to keep the spacing steady. My apprentice asked why the last hole always gets a pause. That's where Gran used to lean over and check my work.

mbm-2773.clue: My mixing bowl pours with a grin.
mbm-2773.quote: I pinched a spout in a clay bowl and left two finger hollows below it. Glaze settled into them like dimples. My nieces only want pancakes poured by the happy bowl.

mbm-2774.clue: One end of the board is the kitchen.
mbm-2774.quote: Our homemade marketplace game runs from the table to the windowsill on a strip of cardboard. My mum charges one biscuit crumb for every piece that crosses the real kitchen. We always pay.

mbm-2775.clue: I know the talking lighthouse is hollow.
mbm-2775.quote: At the mini-golf course my putt went inside the lighthouse and didn't come out. We heard it spiral down for ages. When it rolled free the group behind me applauded the sound effects.
